data.body_html:
January in Marbella might not be beach weather, but it's surprisingly good for a boat charter. With average highs of 16°C, 5 hours of daily sunshine, and calm Mediterranean seas, winter cruising is both comfortable and scenic. This guide covers everything you need to know about Marbella boat rental weather January 2027 – temperatures, sea conditions, which boats work best, and how to book a trip from Puerto Banús.

Marbella January Weather: The Numbers

Marbella enjoys a microclimate thanks to the Sierra Blanca mountains. January averages are as follows:

  • High temperature: 16°C (61°F)
  • Low temperature: 9°C (48°F)
  • Sea temperature: 15°C (59°F)
  • Sunshine: 5 hours per day
  • Rainy days: 7 (mostly light showers)
  • Wind: 10–15 knots, sea state calm to slight

These conditions make January ideal for a relaxed coastal cruise. The sun feels warm by midday, and the lack of summer crowds means you can anchor at spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés almost alone.

Best Boats for a January Charter

For cooler months, boats with enclosed spaces are a smart choice. Our fleet includes several models with heated saloons and flybridges:

  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – large indoor saloon, wrap-around windows.
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) – luxury interior with full heating.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – spacious saloon, plus a free jet ski.
  • Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax) – classic lines, comfortable cabin.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA (21%). You can browse all our Marbella boat rental options for full details.

What to Expect on a January Boat Trip

A typical winter charter lasts 2–4 hours. You'll depart from Puerto Banús and cruise along the coast towards Cabopino or Estepona. The sea is usually flat, with gentle swells under 0.5m. Wildlife sightings – dolphins, seabirds – are common. The light is soft and perfect for photography, with La Concha mountain as a backdrop.

If you choose a Mangusta 80 variant (white or grey), a jet ski is included free for the duration. The cooler air makes riding exhilarating – just bring a wetsuit (we can arrange one).

Pricing for January 2027 Charters

Our pricing is fixed year-round. The most affordable options are Tier A boats:

For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours, with a free jet ski. All other boats – including the Azimut 58 Flybridge, Ferretti 94, Canados 86, and Maiora 26m – are priced on request via WhatsApp.

What to Wear and Bring

Layering is key: a thermal base, fleece, and a windproof jacket. Sunglasses and sunscreen are non-negotiable – the sun reflects off the water even in winter. Non-slip shoes help on deck. If you plan to swim or jet ski, bring a wetsuit (5mm recommended). We provide all drinks and snacks, so just bring yourself.

Why January Is a Great Time to Charter

January is low season in Marbella. That means:

  • Less competition for berths at Puerto Banús.
  • Quieter anchorages – no summer queues.
  • More flexible booking times.
  • Mild temperatures without the July heat.

You'll have the coastline almost to yourself. It's a different, more intimate experience of the Costa del Sol.

Frequently asked questions

Is it warm enough to boat in Marbella in January?

Yes. Daytime highs average 16°C, so it's pleasant on the water with a jacket. The sun feels strong midday, and cabins provide shelter. Many regulars charter in January for the calm seas and fewer crowds.

What is the sea temperature in Marbella in January?

The Mediterranean off Marbella averages 15°C in January. Swimming is possible with a wetsuit; most guests prefer to enjoy the views and stay dry. All our boats have heated indoor spaces.

How many hours of sun does Marbella get in January?

About 5 hours of direct sunshine per day. The sun rises around 08:30 and sets by 18:15, so a midday charter (e.g. 11:00–15:00) maximises daylight and warmth.

Does it rain a lot in Marbella in January?

January averages 7 rainy days, but rainfall is usually light and short. Most days are dry. We monitor forecasts closely and can reschedule if needed.

Which boats are best for a January charter?

Enclosed flybridge or cabin cruisers like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) offer heated interiors. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) also has a large saloon. All depart from Puerto Banús.

Can I swim or do water sports in January?

Swimming is possible with a wetsuit. The Mangusta 80 charters include a free jet ski, which is still fun in cooler weather. Most guests prefer coastal cruising and sightseeing.

What should I wear for a January boat trip?

Layers: a thermal top, fleece or sweater, and a windproof jacket. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still essential – the sun reflects off the water. Non-slip shoes are recommended.

Are January charters cheaper than summer?

Our listed prices are year-round. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749/2h, same as summer. However, availability is better, and you can often book last-minute.
